title: Re-spot the black and the yellow: own spot if free, else the highest-value free spot
instruction: You are the referee. After the foul, the black and the yellow have to be re-spotted; they are on the trays at the two ends of the table. Re-spot both as the rules of snooker require, without moving any other ball on the table, then let go. The discs stand in for the balls.
context: Snooker referees, and club players refereeing their own frames, re-spot colours many times a frame: after a colour is potted while reds remain, forced off the table or potted in a foul. WPBSA Official Rules (May 2022), Section 3 Rule 7: a colour is spotted on its own spot; if that is occupied, on the highest-value spot available; it must not touch another ball. Section 2 Rule 18: a spot is occupied if a ball cannot be placed on it without touching another. A wrong spot changes the frame and is a refereeing error. The skill is a rule-bound judgement read from the table's markings and the colours' values (yellow 2 to black 7), carried out by hand without disturbing any ball. Here the table is a 1:6 model with every spot where the rules put it, all six spots alike and unlabelled, and the two colours wait on trays at the table's two ends; each arm reaches only the tray at its own end.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. A 1:6 model snooker table and nine discs standing for the balls; positions are centres, (x, y) in cm. (1) Bed: a fixed 10 mm thick slab of wood covered in green baize, 296.3 mm along x by 594.8 mm along y (1778 x 3569 mm at full size), centred at (35.0, 0): x 20.18 to 49.82, y -29.74 to +29.74. The baulk end (bottom cushion) is at -y, by the right arm; the top end at +y. (2) Cushions: four fixed wooden rails covered in dark green cloth, 12 mm wide and 20 mm tall on the table (their tops 10 mm above the bed), along the bed's four sides. (3) Markings: white plastic stickers 0.5 mm thick set into the bed, standing 0.2 mm proud. The baulk line, 4 mm wide, across the bed at y -17.46 (737 mm full size from the bottom cushion's face). The D, a 4 mm wide semicircle of radius 48.7 mm (292 mm full size) centred at (35.0, -17.46) on the baulk line, curving toward -y (made of 12 straight strips). Six identical unlabelled 8 mm round spots at (39.87, -17.46) and (30.13, -17.46), the D's two corners; (35.0, -17.46), the middle of the baulk line; (35.0, 0), the table's centre; (35.0, +14.87), midway between the centre and the top cushion's face; and (35.0, +24.34), 54 mm (324 mm full size) from the top cushion's face. (4) Trays: two fixed 60 x 60 x 10 mm wooden slabs centred at (24.0, +37.0), beyond the top end, and (24.0, -37.0), beyond the baulk end. (5) Balls: nine loose rigid plastic discs 30 mm across and 20 mm tall, 25 g each, both faces alike, lying flat, coloured as snooker balls. The black on the top-end tray at (24.0, +37.0); the yellow on the baulk-end tray at (24.0, -37.0). On the bed: a red on the spot at (35.0, +24.34); a red on the spot at (35.0, +14.87); a red at (30.0, +7.0); the pink at (40.0, +9.0); the blue at (30.0, -7.0); the green on the spot at (30.13, -17.46); the brown at (42.0, -10.0). Nothing else is on the table. The discs are over-scale (a ball at 1:6 would be 8.75 mm) so a gripper can hold them; distances are between their centres.
scoring: Judged from the discs' positions (in a real trial: a ruler from the spots' centres and a top photo, after the arms have let go). Disturbance: if any of the seven discs that start on the bed is at any step more than 8 mm (its centre, in 3-D) from where it stood at the start, the score is 0 for the rest of the trial, even if it is put back. Otherwise the black and the yellow are scored separately and added. A colour counts on a spot when all of these hold: its centre is within 8 mm of the spot's centre, seen from above; it lies flat on the bed (tilted under 10 degrees, its lowest point within 3 mm of the bed top, its centre over the bed); no other disc's centre is within 31 mm of its centre, seen from above (the disc's diameter plus 1 mm: it touches no ball and is not stacked, the same test Section 2 Rule 18 uses for an occupied spot); it is released (no gripper's pad-tip point, midway between its finger tips, is lower than 10 mm above the disc's top while within that gripper's finger reach of the disc's axis: 80 mm fully open, 52 mm closed on a disc, at any yaw); and it is still (its centre moved under 1.5 mm in each of the last two 0.5 s windows). Under WPBSA Section 3 Rule 7(e) a colour whose own spot is occupied goes on the highest-value spot available (yellow 2, green 3, brown 4, blue 5, pink 6, black 7). Here reds hold the black's own spot and the pink spot, so the black belongs on the blue spot, the table's centre. Black part: 0.5 counting on the blue spot; 0.25 counting on any other spot (on this table only the brown and yellow spots can be used without touching or moving a ball); 0 otherwise. Yellow part: its own spot is free, so 0.5 counting on the yellow spot (the D's right-hand corner seen from the baulk end, at x 39.87 cm, y -17.46 cm); 0 otherwise. Score = black part + yellow part: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 or 1.0. Every outcome: both right, released and still: 1.0; the black on the brown spot, the yellow right: 0.75; the yellow right and the black on its tray, still gripped, in front of its own occupied spot or anywhere off a spot: 0.5; the black on the blue spot and the yellow on the brown spot, against the green at the D's left corner, or on its tray: 0.5; the black on the brown or yellow spot and the yellow not on its spot: 0.25 (with the black on the yellow spot the yellow cannot count); any bed disc moved over 8 mm (a red pushed off the black spot, the green pushed off its corner, a ball knocked): 0; nothing re-spotted: 0. The trial ends early once 1.0 has held for 2 s; otherwise it is scored on the last step.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, default friction; the bed, cushions, markings and trays are fixed. The table is a 1:6 model and the balls are flat discs about 3.4 times the scaled ball size (30 mm against 8.75 mm) so a gripper can hold them and they cannot roll; occupancy and touching use the disc diameter. The spot positions, the rule that an occupied spot sends a colour to the highest-value free spot and the yellow-on-the-right convention are kept exactly, as a referee would check them.
reset_notes: Put the black back flat on the tray at x 24.0 cm, y +37.0 cm and the yellow on the tray at x 24.0, y -37.0. On the bed stand, flat, a red on each of the spots at (35.0, +24.34) and (35.0, +14.87), a red at (30.0, +7.0), the pink at (40.0, +9.0), the blue at (30.0, -7.0), the green on the spot at (30.13, -17.46) and the brown at (42.0, -10.0) (centres, x and y in cm). The table, cushions, markings and trays are fixed. Nothing is consumed.
